This rule prohibits federal matching funds for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormone therapy, and surgical interventions when used for gender transition for Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. The federal rule is scheduled to take effect on October 13, 2026.
The federal rule does not prohibit states from using state-only funds to cover these services. Maine

Include applicable gender-affirming care diagnosis codes on all claims.
Include the SE modifier on any claims submitted for gender-affirming care, other than behavioral health services.

MaineCare Coverage of Gender-Affirming Care for Medicaid Beneficiaries Under Age 18 and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Enrollees Under Age 19

Oct 09, 2026

As described in the message sent September 18, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 13, 2026, that limits federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for certain gender-affirming care provided to minors. This rule prohibits federal matching funds for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormone therapy, and surgical interventions when used for gender transition for Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. The federal rule is scheduled to take effect on October 13, 2026. 

The federal rule does not prohibit states from using state-only funds to cover these services. Maine law requires MaineCare to cover medically necessary treatment for or related to gender dysphoria and protects members from discrimination based on gender identity or gender expression.   

To ensure we are in compliance with this new federal rule, we have established the billing requirements below for providers who deliver gender-affirming care services to Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. 

Effective on October 13, 2026, medical claims submitted through the MIHMS system must: 

  • Include applicable gender-affirming care diagnosis codes on all claims. 
  • Include the SE modifier on any claims submitted for gender-affirming care, other than behavioral health services.  
    • The SE modifier is used to identify a service that must be reimbursed using state-only funds.  
    • The SE modifier should be listed after any other modifiers on the applicable claim line(s). 
    • Behavioral health treatment for gender dysphoria is still eligible for federal match, so providers are not required to include the SE modifier on behavioral health-related claims.  

Effective on October 9, 2026, pharmacy claims submitted through the MEPOPS system must:  

  • Have Prior Authorization (PA) as required on the Department’s Preferred Drug List. This requirement applies to preferred and non-preferred products on the Department’s identified medication list.   
  • Include the medication’s intended clinical use by including the applicable diagnosis code and the information needed to determine the appropriate coverage and funding pathway.  
    • Medication prescribed for a clinical use outside the scope of 42 CFR § 441.801–441.802 and 457.476 remains subject to the otherwise applicable MaineCare pharmacy criteria. For medication prescribed for use within the scope of those provisions, the Department will review coverage under its separately funded state-only benefit.  

This PA requirement is used to determine clinical purpose and payment source. It does not, by itself, change the drug’s preferred status, establish additional step therapy, or mean that all uses of the medication are excluded from federally matched coverage. Existing drug-specific clinical criteria continue to apply as appropriate.  

For questions, please contact Provider Relations Specialist, Lisa Bouchard.

New MaineCare Partner Portal: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements

Oct 06, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and will require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Read below for more information and steps you will need to take to sign into the MaineCare Partner Portal starting on October 12. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the “HealthPAS Online Portal” section of the Provider Resources page.  

Multi-Factor Authenticator (MFA) 

MFA adds a second verification step after entering your password. This is an important new security measure to protect the sensitive information held in the Portal. You will have three options to choose from for your additional authentication factor; you must choose one.

Follow the instructions below for first-time setup of the option you choose. 

  1. Microsoft Authenticator 

The Microsoft Authenticator app is the recommended MFA method because it offers the highest level of protection over other methods. Download the Microsoft Authenticator app now on a smartphone or tablet so that you are ready to use it on October 12. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via the app:  

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Open the Microsoft Authenticator app. 
  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Click the QR code scanner in the Microsoft Authenticator app and scan the QR code displayed on the Portal’s User Details window.  

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Text/Call 

Text (SMS) or call verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027.  

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via text (SMS) or call: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Text/call” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter a phone number, request a code or call, then verify the code. The phone number you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Email 

Email verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via email: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Email” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter an email address, request a code, then verify the code. The email address you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process. 

 

For additional instructions on both initial setup and ongoing use of MFA, including screenshots, please reference the job aid MaineCare Partner Portal MFA Setup and Access Job Aid. 

  • You can find this job aid and other supporting resources through the MMIS Learning Center. Search for the course “ME – MIHMS Upgrade Documentation,” enroll in the course, then look for the job aid in the documentation list. 
  • Starting October 12, 2026, this job aid will also be available in the MaineCare Partner Portal under the Provider tab > Provider Manuals subtab. 

Need Help? 

If you have questions about these instructions, please call Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. 

Thank you for preparing in advance for a smooth transition to the new MaineCare Partner Portal.

Pursuant to MBM, Ch. I, Section 1.18 failure to comply with these requirements can result in the denial of claims or recoupment of payment because services delivered without proper state licensure are not eligible for reimbursement.

Looking Ahead: Eligibility-Dedicated Data Feed to Support MaineCare Renewals and Enrollment

Sep 04, 2026

Two weeks ago, we announced communications support for MaineCare partners and providers regarding changes the federal government is making to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program) eligibility. This message provides an early look at planned data-sharing that will help the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) verify information needed for MaineCare eligibility. Our goal is to help eligible Mainers keep their coverage and access to services with as little disruption as possible.

No action is needed now. We are sharing this information early to make providers aware of what is being planned. We will share more information as plans and timelines are finalized.

DHHS will continue to use administrative data sources it has access to as much as possible to support automatic (“passive”) renewals for MaineCare members. Federal changes to eligibility mean we need additional information to help more eligible members maintain their MaineCare coverage. This data will help Mainers continue to benefit from MaineCare, which in turn will help providers minimize the impact of these federal Medicaid cuts on their revenue and on their charity and uncompensated care.

Clinical Data Will Help People Stay Enrolled in MaineCare

Electronic health record (EHR) systems contain clinical data that Maine and numerous other states are planning to use to help exempt Medicaid applicants and members with work-limiting health conditions from Work Requirements. In Maine, this data will support MaineCare eligibility determination activities administered by the Office for Family Independence (OFI). DHHS intends to partner with providers to collect this information through HealthInfoNet, the State’s contractor for this work. HealthInfoNet will identify indicators of exemptions from work requirements by collecting and processing this clinical data from providers. Using clinical data alongside claims and other administrative data to generate more timely and comprehensive information will help keep Mainers enrolled in MaineCare. We will refer to the data sent to HealthInfoNet for this purpose as the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed.

Until the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed is established we will be basing automatic exceptions for work-limiting health conditions on claims data alone in order to meet implementation deadlines.

This Data Sharing Will Be Separate from the Health Information Exchange

The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be separate from the health information exchange (HIE) data that many providers already share with HealthInfoNet.

The eligibility-dedicated data feed will include only the information needed to support MaineCare eligibility activities. This information will be stored separately from HIE data. It will not be available through HealthInfoNet’s clinical portal or through analytics tools used by some provider organizations. The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be used only in support of OMS and OFI activities associated with eligibility.

Key details to note:

  • The steps needed for a provider to establish this new data feed will vary by provider organization. For example, some provider organizations already have a data feed with HealthInfoNet that can be used as a starting point. Capabilities of the organization’s EHR vendor or technology support may also affect the work needed to establish the data feed. Providers eligible for relevant Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding may consider using this funding for these costs, as determined by the allowable uses of specific RHTP opportunities.
  • We expect it will take the majority of provider organizations two to four months to build their eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed with HealthInfoNet. This time range will be dependent on provider organization’s or vendor’s availability to engage with HealthInfoNet. We expect it will take less time than building a typical HIE data sharing connection with HealthInfoNet.
  • Clinical care teams are not expected to need to take additional steps to send this information as part of their day-to-day work. Once the data feed is established, the identified data categories will be shared automatically with HealthInfoNet.
  • Broad categories of exemptions in statute for work-limiting health conditions include those who are blind or disabled, have a substance use disorder, disabling mental disorder, or complex medical condition. DHHS continues to work with the federal government to clarify data related to these categories that may assist states to automatically exempt individuals, including information related to a person’s ability to work. Kinds of data may include demographic information, diagnosis indicators, encounter or event indicators, and billing codes, among others.

More Information Will Be Coming – No Action Needed Now The Department and HealthInfoNet will distribute instructions for provider organizations to opt into this initiative and implement the eligibility-dedicated data feed. Future communications will include information such as:

  • Which provider types will be prioritized for establishing these connections
  • How providers can participate
  • The types of information that will be needed
  • Technical requirements and specifications
  • Onboarding and implementation steps
  • Timelines
  • Testing procedures
  • Contacts for technical and operational qu

The conference welcomes participants in all roles with MaineCare provider organizations, including:

  • Program staff
  • Quality improvement professionals
  • Other team members who support MaineCare members

Notice of Agency Rulemaking Proposal

 

AGENCY: Department of Health and Human Services, Office of MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Ch. III, Sec. 20, Allowances for Home and Community-Based Services for Adults with Other Related Conditions

TYPE OF RULE: Major Substantive

BRIEF SUMMARY: Section 20 in the MBM authorizes home and community-based services (HCBS) under a CMS-approved Section 1915(c) waiver. The Department proposes to amend the Chapter III, Section 20 rule to establish the reimbursement methodology for new services being added under a companion, Chapter II, Section 20 rule, and to remove rates of reimbursement for all services which will now be listed in Rate Schedules on the Department’s website pursuant to 22 M.R.S. § 3177-J. The website address for current rates of reimbursement in the Department’s website and the statutory authority for this approach is stated in this proposed rule. Procedure codes, modifiers, and billable units remain in the rule, together with provisions for annual cost of living adjustments in conformance with 22 M.R.S. § 3173-J(2)(D)(3). Such cost-of-living adjustments will satisfy the requirements for direct support worker wages set forth in 22 M.R.S. § 7402(1).

See http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/oms/rules/index.shtml for rules and related rulemaking documents.

Once adopted, the proposed Chapter III, Section 20 rule will only be provisional: as a major substantive rule, Chapter III, Section 20 requires Legislative approval before it can be legally effective. Therefore, the Department anticipates also adopting an emergency Chapter III, Section 20 rule so that these methodology and rates changes will become legally effective on the same date as changes to the Chapter II, Section 20 routine technical rule becomes effective.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 25, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.

    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.
